entities.title: datetime.date examples
entities.summary: What datetime.date does for each date task (construction, range, parsing, weekday numbering, ISO week, arithmetic, ordering), compared with CivilDate.
criteria: The date constructor creates the date when the fields name a real day.
The date constructor raises a ValueError when the day does not exist in the month.
The date constructor raises a ValueError when the month is 13.
The date constructor raises a ValueError when the year is beyond 9999.
The date constructor raises a ValueError when the year is before year 1.
date.max is the last day of year 9999.
date.fromisoformat reads the date when the text is an ISO 8601 calendar date.
date.fromisoformat raises a ValueError when the text names a day that does not exist.
date.weekday numbers Sunday 6, counting from Monday 0, when the date is a Sunday.
date.isoweekday numbers Sunday 7, as ISO 8601 does, when the date is a Sunday.
date.isocalendar returns the ISO 8601 week number of the date.
Adding a timedelta to a date returns the date that many days later, carrying into the next month.
date.replace raises a ValueError when the day is missing from the target month.
Subtracting two dates gives a timedelta whose days are the number of days between them.
date's less-than operator is true when the left date comes first.

entities.title: datetime.datetime examples
entities.summary: Naive and aware datetimes, now, parsing Z and +00:00, timestamps, arithmetic across DST, astimezone in gaps and overlaps, ordering and the round trip through UTV.
criteria: The datetime constructor creates a naive wall time when given no tzinfo.
The datetime constructor raises a ValueError when the second is a leap second, 60.
The datetime constructor pins the wall time to the offset when given a fixed timezone.
datetime.now returns a naive wall time, of this machine's zone, when given no tz.
datetime.now with timezone.utc returns a reading that UTV takes as an input without changing it.
datetime.fromisoformat gives the same value for text ending in Z and text ending in +00:00.
datetime.fromtimestamp returns the Unix epoch when given zero seconds and timezone.utc.
datetime.fromtimestamp keeps only six fractional digits, rounded, when given a timestamp with nine.
datetime.timestamp returns the seconds since the epoch as a float.
Subtracting two datetimes gives a timedelta whose total_seconds is a float.
Subtracting two datetimes with the same ZoneInfo subtracts their wall times, ignoring a daylight-saving change between them.
Adding a timedelta to a datetime carries into the next day when the hours pass midnight.
Adding a day to a datetime with a ZoneInfo keeps the wall time and takes the new offset when the day crosses a daylight-saving change.
Adding a day to a datetime with a fixed timezone keeps the offset, so across a daylight-saving change the wall time in New York becomes 13:00.
datetime.astimezone(timezone.utc) returns the instant when the wall time happens exactly once.
datetime.astimezone returns the local wall time when given a ZoneInfo.
datetime.astimezone converts a wall time that falls in a daylight-saving gap without a word, as if the clocks had not changed yet.
datetime.astimezone picks the earlier, daylight-time instant through fold=0, silently, when the wall time happens twice.
datetime's less-than operator compares wall times, ignoring fold, when both datetimes share a ZoneInfo.
datetime's == is true when the value made a round trip through UTV.

criteria: ZoneInfo.utcoffset returns the offset in force before the change, without a word, when the wall time falls in a daylight-saving gap.

ZoneInfo.utcoffset returns the standard-time offset when the wall time happens twice and fold is 1.
